candidate_relations.reason: Congenital Granular Cell Tumor is widely considered synonymous or near-synonymous with congenital granular cell epulis in most literature, but 'epulis' anchors the diagnosis to the alveolar ridge location and neonatal context. Some authors treat CGCT as a broader category. This is at minimum a very close partial match, arguably complete equivalent depending on classification system used.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Congenital Granular Cell Tumor is the broader/alternative name used in some classifications; 'epulis' specifies the gingival/alveolar ridge location and neonatal presentation context, making CGCE the preferred specific term

candidate_relations.label: Myofibroma
candidate_relations.reason: Myofibroma does not match the clinical or histological profile of congenital granular cell epulis; different cell of origin and histopathology.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Myofibroma is a distinct mesenchymal tumor with different histology (myofibroblastic differentiation)

candidate_relations.reason: The lesions described are large, pedunculated, solid swellings up to 3.5 cm, inconsistent with small gingival cysts of the newborn.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Gingival cysts of the newborn (Epstein pearls/Bohn nodules) are small keratin-filled cysts, not pedunculated solid masses

candidate_relations.reason: Lymphangioma would show different clinical and histological features; the firm, solid, pedunculated alveolar masses in this case are characteristic of congenital granular cell epulis, not lymphangioma.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Lymphangioma is a vascular/lymphatic malformation, not a granular cell lesion

candidate_relations.reason: The lesions are described as firm and pink, not consistent with the typical soft, compressible, bluish-red appearance of hemangioma; different entity entirely.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Hemangioma is a vascular tumor with distinct histology

candidate_relations.reason: Same reasoning as C003; neonatal gingival cysts are tiny, self-resolving cystic structures, not the large solid pedunculated masses described here.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Neonatal gingival cyst is essentially the same as C003 — small cystic lesions, not large solid pedunculated masses

candidate_relations.reason: LCH does not present as multiple pedunculated alveolar masses in a neonate; entirely different pathological entity.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Langerhans Cell Histiocytosis is a systemic histiocytic disorder with different histology and clinical behavior

candidate_relations.reason: MNTI is a differential diagnosis for alveolar ridge masses in infants but has distinct histological features (melanin-containing cells, neuroblast-like cells) and is not equivalent to congenital granular cell epulis.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Melanotic neuroectodermal tumor of infancy also occurs on the alveolar ridge of neonates but is a distinct entity with pigmented cells and different histology

candidate_relations.reason: Teratoma is a germ cell tumor with multi-tissue composition; not consistent with the clinical presentation or expected histology of congenital granular cell epulis.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Teratoma contains elements from multiple germ layers; entirely different entity

candidate_relations.reason: Congenital Epulis is the standard clinical synonym for congenital granular cell epulis; in the neonatal setting with alveolar ridge location, these terms are used interchangeably in the literature and represent the same diagnostic entity.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: 'Congenital Epulis' is the classic, widely accepted synonym for congenital granular cell epulis in the neonatal alveolar ridge context

case_quality_flags: C001 (Congenital Granular Cell Tumor) and C010 (Congenital Epulis) are near-synonymous with the reference; C001 rated partial due to lack of site-specific 'epulis' qualifier in some classification systems, though many authors treat them as identical
